title: Club Membership: computing the outstanding balance available for a medical-hold waiver
content:
## Scope
This document states how Club Membership computes the outstanding balance that a medical-hold dues waiver may waive, before any employer-funded share is taken into account.

## Rule
The outstanding balance available to waive is computed as the sum of every dues charge ever billed to the contract that is either the one-time enrollment fee charge or a recurring dues charge, minus the sum of every payment amount ever applied to the contract, minus the sum of every waiver amount already granted to the contract. A late fee charge or an early-termination fee charge on this same contract is never folded into this sum, since each is itself the billed amount of a different problem. This balance is evaluated at the moment the waiver is processed, so that any enrollment fee or recurring dues charge posted earlier in the same consultation is included in the sum.

## Prerequisite: the enrollment fee charge must already be posted
This policy's own basis holds that the one-time enrollment fee charge for this contract must already be posted to the ledger before the outstanding balance available to waive is computed; where it is not yet posted, the outstanding balance available to waive is not yet complete and this waiver is not handled.

## Prerequisite: this cycle's recurring dues charge must already be posted
This policy's own basis likewise holds that this billing cycle's recurring dues charge for this contract must already be posted to the ledger before the outstanding balance available to waive is computed; where it is not yet posted, the outstanding balance available to waive is not yet complete and this waiver is not handled.

## Points of judgement
A payment applied to the contract before the waiver is processed reduces this outstanding balance dollar for dollar; a waiver already granted to the contract earlier likewise reduces it dollar for dollar, so the same portion of the balance is never waived twice.
